title: BEETL Competition 2021 Motor Imagery Dataset A — transfer learning benchmark
description: The BEETL Competition 2021 Motor Imagery Dataset A is a transfer learning benchmark comprising EEG recordings from 3 healthy subjects performing four-class motor imagery tasks (rest, left hand, right hand, feet) in an online brain-computer interface racing game. Recorded at 500 Hz with 63 channels and preprocessed with bandpass (1-100 Hz) and notch (50 Hz) filtering, this dataset addresses the challenge of cross-subject and cross-dataset generalization in motor imagery decoding, serving as a benchmark for evaluating transfer learning and domain adaptation techniques in biosignal machine learning.
methods_description: EEG data were collected at 500 Hz sampling rate using 63 channels in a standard 1005 montage during an online Cybathlon2020IC racing game. Subjects performed four motor imagery tasks (rest, left hand, right hand, feet) with 4-second trial duration. Data preprocessing included bandpass filtering (1-100 Hz) and 50 Hz notch filtering. Training data comprised 5 races per subject and testing data comprised 10 races per subject, with each race containing multiple 4-second trials. The competition evaluated transfer learning from multiple source datasets (Cho2017, BNCI2014, PhysionetMI) to target datasets with different EEG setups and electrode configurations.
